# 3.5 Grid and counting DP modulo a prime

Phase 3 (Recursion to dynamic programming), target rating 1500–1900. Bank status: short.

## Patterns

### Counting paths in a grid (`grid-paths`)

Number of right/down paths through a grid with blocked cells, modulo a prime.

**Works because:** Moves form an acyclic order on the cells, so each cell's count is the sum of its predecessors' counts.

### Counting sequences (`sequence-counting`)

Count sequences or strings satisfying local rules, modulo a prime.

**Works because:** Whether a sequence can be extended depends only on a small state (last element, current sum).

### Ordered and unordered sums (`partition-counting`)

Count ways to write n as a sum of allowed parts, either as ordered sequences or as multisets.

**Works because:** For unordered sums the loop over part types is outside the loop over totals, so each multiset is counted once.

### Transitions over a range (`range-sum-transition`)

dp[i] is the sum of dp[j] over a contiguous range of j; keep prefix sums of dp to make each transition O(1).

**Works because:** The set of predecessors is a contiguous range of indices.
